pages.text: Thud! Yuki's thrown snowball hit brown dog Momo's back. Momo yelped and backed to the wall. "Oh... I didn't mean to." Yuki froze with the throwing arm still out.
Momo sat by the wall and stared, ears drooping. The words "I'm sorry" stayed inside Yuki's mouth. Yuki hid both hands in their sleeves and turned away.
Yuki only kicked at snow. Playing was no fun. Momo stayed still by the wall. The yard was quiet, and the distance between them seemed large.
Grandma came outside and stood beside Yuki. "Why keep hiding your hands?" Yuki gripped the sleeves tighter. "...I don't know."
"Momo can't see a sorry feeling hidden in your sleeves." Grandma gently rolled them back and brought Yuki's hands out.
One step, two steps toward the wall. Yuki crouched before Momo and met their eyes. "I'm sorry I threw that snowball."
Then a hand reached to stroke Momo's back, softly. Momo waved their tail and nuzzled Yuki's hand. "Say Sorry, Then Stroke Gently!"
With the hidden hands out, Yuki's heart felt light. Momo jumped up and circled Yuki. Both ran around the yard again.
While running, Yuki accidentally stepped on Momo's front paw. Yelp! Yuki fixed the slipping scarf knot and quickly crouched. "One, look in the eyes and say sorry! Two, stroke with my hand!"
Grandma drew Yuki close and hugged their shoulders. "Hiding a sorry feeling makes it heavy. Saying it makes it light." Yuki stroked Momo's back again. "Say Sorry, Then Stroke Gently!"
